title: 16th Sitting of second session of 2025
summary: After routine opening business, the Kudahuvadhoo member introduced the government's Maldives Intellectual Property Office Bill, which would create an office, led by a Registrar, to register and protect trademarks, patents, copyright and similar creations. Thirteen members debated it: most backed the aim of protecting young creators, while several worried about extra cost and about the Registrar being appointed and removed by a minister, and many also used the debate to criticise the economy, the dollar shortage and ministers not answering the Majlis. After a break, debate began on the government's Trademarks Bill. Part of this text is garbled and the part ends mid-speech, so no vote is recorded here. This part finishes the debate on the government's Trademark Bill, which members discussed together with the Maldives Intellectual Property Office Bill. Government-side members backed the bills as protection for local traders against fake goods, while Hanimaadhoo and South Hulhumale' members raised concerns about spending and about Maldivian fish being sold under foreign brands. After the sponsor's closing remarks, the Judiciary Committee's report on candidates for a public seat on the Judicial Service Commission was presented with no debate, and three votes followed: both bills were accepted and sent to the Economic Committee, and Idrees Fauz was approved for the Commission. The sitting closed with the next one set for Monday 21 July 2025 at 9:00. The part opens mid-speech by a member whose name appears in the previous part, so that turn is not counted here.

items.title: Sitting closed and next sitting announced

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Said the Trademarks Bill is not bad and registering marks is needed, but another office adds spending.
Asked about priorities such as hospital services, water and sewerage and the dollar shortage.
Said he does not object to trademark registration but questioned spending on a drone show and an airport opening while Kulhudhuffushi hospital lacks doctors and medicine.
Was asked by the chair to keep to the topic of the bill and was told his party's allotted time had run out.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Said the bill is important but questioned a new institution; suggested running it within a ministry to save cost.
Raised jobless Maldivian pilots and the dollar rate rising on the black market, and called on the MMA governor to act.
After a point of order from the Majlis Majority Leader, said he was being heckled and asked to speak.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Introduced the Intellectual Property Office Bill: a registry and office to protect creations of artists, young people and innovators, with a Registrar and five chapters.
In closing, thanked the President for sending the bill through legal channels and said it sets out international cooperation and could give young creators work.
Said the cost concern is outweighed by new opportunities for young creators and reduced demand for government jobs.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Backed the bill as supporting the economy and helping Maldivian brands compete abroad; urged committee to consult artists and experts.
On the Trademarks Bill, said both bills are important and overdue, and that registration gives young creators legal certainty.
Said critics underestimate young Maldivians' creativity.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Concerned that articles 7 and 13 let the minister appoint and remove the Registrar and supply staff; preferred an independent body or a ministry unit.
Said the bill shows no source of income for the office and may add political appointees.
On the Trademarks Bill, said opposition members are rivals not enemies, and cited unanswered Right to Information requests and ministers not attending Majlis questions.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Thanked the government and noted the 2010 copyright law; hoped committee would change the minister-only appointment of the Registrar.
Raised the dollar shortage, unpaid contractors, ceremony spending and unmet service needs such as medicine and pedestrian crossing lights.
Raised concern that a Chinese company marketing canned Maldivian fish could cause problems for fish exports under trademark rules, and urged that Maldivian fish not be tied up abroad.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Raised a point of order objecting to false allegations by the Velidhoo member; the chair accepted it as a point of order and asked for respect.
On the Trademarks Bill, said it is a large 52-article bill and that debate had drifted to other topics.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Supported the bill and said spending and dollar complaints by others are not about this bill; defended the government's policies.
Defended spending on the airport and a bridge; the chair asked him to keep to the bill's subject.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Supported the bill as protecting traders and sole agents from counterfeit goods.
Said some opposition members gave the public a misleading picture of hospital medicine, Aasandha and state finances.
Was twice asked by the chair to speak on the bill's topic.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Supported the bill as giving young creators a legal framework and said earlier laws lacked implementation detail that this bill provides.
Said intellectual property covers trademarks, copyright, patents, industrial designs and geographical indications, and thanked the government for bringing it.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Said protecting intellectual property is useful but the economy is stalled, small businesses cannot get finance and the dollar rate keeps rising.
Raised the shift of resort service charge to rufiyaa and called for the MMA governor to be summoned to the Majlis.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Supported the bill as protecting traders and exports; said the dollar rate and service charge issues are not caused by the lack of this law.
Compared exchange rates under past governments and defended the current government's economic work.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Thanked the sponsor and said the bill brings positive change; asked committee to consult all stakeholders and give the bill a Dhivehi name.
Said another office adds costs in the current economy and urged opposition parties not to talk the economy down.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Supported the bill as protecting artists, scientists and industrial and digital creators, and thanked the government for sending it.
Said some members mislead the public by speaking of other issues.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Said the aim is not bad but he sees no need now and opposes extra spending on a new office.
Said basic services such as water and sewerage are missing on islands and ministers do not answer.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Explained what intellectual property is and the role of WIPO, and supported the bill as a start to collective management of creators' rights.
Said it needs funding and thanked the sponsor.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the bill as important for the future and said the recent innovation expo showed local talent.
Suggested a digital transactions law so Maldivian products can be sold on platforms like Amazon, and funding for young inventors.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Fully supported the Trademarks Bill and said Maldives joined WIPO in 2004 but still lacks these laws.
Said Maldivian designs and national symbols are sold online unprotected and creators register firms abroad, losing income to the economy.

speakers.name: Ali Fazad
positions: Said intellectual property laws matter for the economy but weak enforcement is the main problem; urged deeper committee study.
Described the trademark, copyright and IP laws together as the economic foundation.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Supported the bill as protection for local traders against counterfeit goods such as fake energy drinks, and for the losses those goods cause.
Rejected the claim that the government is selling the Maldivian fish brand abroad.
Said opposition talk of new offices and higher spending does not address traders' problems.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Backed the bills as making business safer and easier for traders, and said an intellectual property office is standard practice worldwide.
Rejected the opposition's argument that new offices raise state spending.
Said parliament shares responsibility with the president for making independent institutions work.

speakers.name: Ahmed Zahir
positions: As the bill's sponsor, said trademarks protect brand names and logos while copyright covers books and software, so one law cannot replace the other.
Said a patents bill is expected to follow, and cited older trademark laws in the UK, US, Sri Lanka and India.
Thanked members who debated and urged the bill become law quickly.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: As Judiciary Committee rapporteur, reported that 8 people applied for the Judicial Service Commission public seat, 2 withdrew and 6 were interviewed; those scoring above 75 percent were found suitable, and asked the house to decide.

decisions: Maldives Intellectual Property Office Bill: first reading given and preliminary debate closed after the sponsor's closing remarks.
Vote on accepting the Intellectual Property Office Bill left for the sitting's voting time (not in this part).
Recess taken from 10:31 to 11:02 during debate on the Trademarks Bill; debate continued after.
The Maldives Intellectual Property Office Bill (sponsor: Hussain Hameed, Kudahuvadhoo) was accepted in principle and sent to the Economic Committee for review.
The Trademark Bill (sponsor: Ahmed Zahir, Maduvvari) was accepted in principle and sent to the Economic Committee for review.
The Judiciary Committee's report on Judicial Service Commission candidates was presented; no member asked to debate it.
The house approved the appointment of Idrees Fauz (Kalaidhoo) as the public member of the Judicial Service Commission.
The next sitting was set for Monday 21 July 2025 at 9:00.

votes.what: Accepting the Maldives Intellectual Property Office Bill (sponsor: Hussain Hameed, Kudahuvadhoo)
Accepting the Trademark Bill (sponsor: Ahmed Zahir, Maduvvari)
Appointing Idrees Fauz as the public member of the Judicial Service Commission
